title: Chef Vikas Khanna Raises Funds and Spirits at Atlanta Gala for Leap to Shine
excerpt: The Michelin-starred chef and 2026 TIME100 honoree headlined an intimate fundraising dinner in Atlanta to support digital education for underserved children across India
body:
• Michelin-starred chef Vikas Khanna headlined an intimate fundraising gala in Atlanta on August 10, raising funds for Leap to Shine, a nonprofit that provides digital education tools to underserved children in India.
  • Khanna was honored with the Global Humanitarian Icon Award by Leap to Shine for his sustained work supporting education and digital learning for children in underserved communities.
  • Leap to Shine has reached over 3,200 students and distributed 661 tablets and laptops across 17 projects in 8 Indian states, with 90 percent of every dollar going directly to programs.
  • Khanna, who was named to the 2026 TIME100 list of the world's most influential people, has used his culinary platform to champion causes ranging from girls' education to large-scale food relief.

Indian-American chef Vikas Khanna brought his trademark blend of culinary artistry and humanitarian passion to Atlanta on August 10, headlining an intimate fundraising gala for Leap to Shine, the nonprofit he has championed for years in its mission to bridge the digital education divide for children across India.

The evening, billed as "An Intimate Evening with Chef Vikas Khanna," featured a banquet-style three-course dinner, a fireside chat with Khanna, and a celebration of Indian cuisine and culture — all in service of a cause that has become central to the chef's public life.

Global Humanitarian Icon

At the gala, Leap to Shine honored Khanna with its Global Humanitarian Icon Award, recognizing his sustained commitment to supporting underserved children through education and digital access. The New Jersey-based nonprofit has focused its efforts on closing the gap between potential and opportunity for students who lack basic learning tools.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=VE4djGlA37I

To date, Leap to Shine has empowered more than 3,200 students and distributed 661 tablets and laptops across 17 projects in eight Indian states. The organization says 90 percent of every dollar raised goes directly to programs rather than overhead.

From TIME100 to the Fundraising Floor

Khanna arrived at the Atlanta gala fresh off being named to the 2026 TIME100, TIME magazine's annual list of the world's most influential people. Eric Ripert, the celebrated French chef, wrote Khanna's profile for the list, noting that his influence lies "not only in success but in uplifting and connecting with others."

An eight-time Michelin-starred chef, restaurateur, and author of more than 41 books, Khanna has built a career that straddles high cuisine and social impact. His New York City restaurant Bungalow has become a cultural tribute to India, while his humanitarian initiatives — including distributing over 30 million meals across 135 Indian cities during the COVID-19 pandemic — have earned him recognition far beyond the kitchen.

"Education is a weapon that allows every child to stand shoulder to shoulder with the world."

— Vikas Khanna

Bridging the Digital Divide

This year's fundraising drive spotlighted two featured projects. The first, a Higher Education Scholarship Program run in partnership with CORP India in Mumbai, supports 17 students — many of them young women — who have completed Class 12 by covering college and coaching fees and pairing them with mentorship and career guidance.

Khanna's connection to education access runs deep. His short documentary "Barefoot Empress," produced with Oscar-nominated filmmaker Doug Roland, chronicles the story of 96-year-old Karthyayani Amma of Kerala, who joined a first-grade class and scored 98 out of 100. The film inspired Leap to Shine's pledge to educate five million girls in India.

For the Indian-American community, the Atlanta gala was both a celebration and a call to action — a reminder that the diaspora's growing influence carries with it a responsibility to the millions of children in India for whom a tablet or a scholarship can mean the difference between a stalled dream and an open door.
nri_angle: Indian-American chef Vikas Khanna leverages his global platform to mobilize the NRI community around education access in India, raising funds at an Atlanta gala that highlights the diaspora's role in bridging opportunities for underserved children back home.
